Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serve as the Antiterrorism Officer (ATO), GS-0301-12 for Garrison Antiterrorism (AT) program in support of the Force Protection (FP) mission. Works under the Chief of Protection in the Directorate of Plans, Training, Mobilization and Security (DPTMS). It is located in Boebligen, in the Stuttgart region of Germany on Panzerkaserne base.
Details.SubAgencyName: US Army Garrsion Stuttgart, S 3/5/7, Plans/Operations Division
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, its impressive gardens and parks, palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles, but also by its cultural diversity. The city of Stuttgart comprises five counties encompassing 179 towns and rural districts. It is the home to USAG Stuttgart, HQ US EUCOM, HQ US AFRICOM, and other tenant units. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/
MajorDuties: Conduct comprehensive review and analysis of the garrison's AT plan, assessments, and survey reports for compliance with existing policies, procedures and supporting documents.
Direct the development, implementation, and operation of an integrated AT program.
Oversee the FP Fusion Cell and AT/FP Working Group and advise the garrison Crisis Management Team.
Advise Chief of Protection and DPTMS of AT and FP deficiencies that would affect the FP posture of the garrison.

Plan, coordinate, schedule and conduct, and or facilitate AT Working Groups, Committees, Executive Councils, Threat Working Groups, and when necessary or required, any other meetings regarding the garrison AT program.
Coordinate with the garrison Resource Management Office to plan, program and execute the AT budget through the Schedule 75, Plans, Programs Budget Execution Program (cradle to grave budget planning).

Responsible for ensuring the garrison threat statement remains current, is included in the garrison AT plan, and is used to develop the garrison AT plan to deter, defend against and defeat the threat.
Represent garrison at meetings, conferences, and seminars with AT representatives of DoD.

If an employee brings a child to an overseas location and that child is entitled to attend a DoD school on a space-required basis in accordance with DoDEA Regulation 1342.13, the DoDEA and the Military Department responsible for providing related services will ensure that the child, if eligible for special education, receives a free appropriate public education, including related services pursuant to DoDI 1342.12 and DoDM 1342.12. If an employee brings an infant or toddler (up to 3 years of age) to an overseas location, and that infant or toddler, but for the child's age, is entitled to attend the DoDEA on a space-required basis in accordance with DoDEA Regulation 1342.13, then the Military Department responsible for EIS will provide the infant or toddler with the required EIS in accordance with the eligibility criteria consistent with DoDI 1342.12 and DoDM 1342.12. Employees (and family members) who require medical or dental care in the overseas location will be responsible for obtaining and paying for such care. Access for civilian employees and their families to military medical and dental treatment facilities is on a space-available and reimbursable basis only. Pay retention may be offered to selected applicants for positions at overseas locations. Pay retention will not be offered as an incentive for employees moving between overseas positions. Selectees may receive certain foreign area benefits such as: Living Quarters Allowance (LQA) or government quarters, home leave, etc. Selectees will have their eligibility for foreign area benefits determined at the time of hire in accordance with Department of State Standardized Regulation (DSSR) and DoDI 1400.25 volume 1250. For positions in a foreign country, that country's laws or international agreements may have a direct impact on the ability of an employee's same sex domestic partner or spouse to accompany the employee and receive certain benefits. If you believe you may be affected by these laws and agreements, you should familiarize yourself with relevant information and direct questions concerning a specific country (Foreign Duty Location) to the appropriate Army Human Resources point of contact prior to the acceptance of employment and your entrance on duty. This is a Force Protection and Anti-Terrorism Career Field position. The initial length of this overseas tour is 36 months. Defense National Relocation Program will not be authorized. Multiple positions may be filled from this announcement. When you perform a Civilian Permanent Change of Station (PCS) with the government, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) considers the majority of your entitlements to be taxable. Visit https://www.dfas.mil/civilianemployees/civrelo/Civilian-Moving-Expenses-Tax-Deduction/ for more information. Payment of Permanent Change of Station (PCS) costs is authorized, subject to the provisions of the Joint Travel Regulations.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.SubAgency: Headquarters United States Africa Command (AFRICOM), Command Directorate, J0
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Position may be filled as a Term Appointment Not to Exceed (NTE) 3 YEARS. Term appointments may be extended beyond of six (6) years, up to eight (8) years. With DoD approval, Term appointments may be extended beyond eight (8) years. Current permanent Federal employees (to include permanent Army employees) applying for Term appointment will be appointed/converted into a Term appointment with no statutory return rights back to a permanent position. Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Applying to OCONUS Positions Current Department of Defense (DOD) Civilian Employee (non-Army) Excepted Service Overseas Family Member Appointment Family Member Preference (FMP) for Overseas Employment Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Military Spouse Preference (MSP) for Overseas Employment Non-Department of Defense (DoD) Transfer Reinstatement Veterans Recruitment Appointment (VRA) In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes 1) Executing program(s) such as family readiness, quality of life, family issues, social problems, and/or related programs; AND 2) Coordinating and/or marketing program information, training, and/or volunteer activities; AND 3) Cooperating with leaders, beneficiaries, and/or the community in support of a family or quality of life program; AND 4) Performing administrative tasks utilizing office automation software and equipment. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07 or above). You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Administration and Management Communications Customer Service Project Management Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-07).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position may be filled as a Term Appointment Not To Exceed (NTE) 3 years. The incumbent serves as a Military and Family Readiness Specialist within a four-star level joint command in support of a more senior, geographically separated workforce that is largely stationary without unit forward deployments. Provides general oversight and advice to Molesworth (U.K.) and Combined Joint Task Force - Horn (CJTF-HOA) in family readiness programs.
Details.SubAgencyName: Headquarters United States Africa Command (AFRICOM), Command Directorate, J0
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/ United States Africa Command (USAFRICOM), is one of six U.S. Department of Defense' geographic combatant commands and is responsible to the Secretary of Defense for military relations with African nations, the African Union, and African regional security organizations. It is responsible for all DoD operations, exercises, and security cooperation on the African continent, its island nations, and surrounding waters. Its mission is to build defense capabilities, respond to crisis, and deter and defeat transnational threats in order to advance U.S. national interests and promote regional security, stability, and prosperity.
MajorDuties: Coordinate all actions and functions related to the management of the service member and family readiness group in accordance with the AR 608-1.

Liaise on behalf of the Combatant Commander under the guidance of the Headquarters Commandant, with SFRG leaders, community service agencies, chaplains, and other activities to share knowledge on family readiness matters and support services.
Performs administrative duties using a variety of office equipment and software.
Plans, coordinate, and execute major U.S. Africa Command sponsored family events, tours, conferences, and trainings.

If, after reviewing your resume and/or supporting documentation, a determination is made that you have inflated your qualifications and/or experience, you may lose consideration for this position. Please follow all instructions carefully when applying, errors or omissions may affect your eligibility. The selecting official has requested a competitive and noncompetitive candidate list for this vacancy. If you are eligible for the noncompetitive list, you will be evaluated on basic and/or minimum qualifications, as applicable. While required to answer the assessment questions, non-competitive candidates will not be evaluated against the competitive rating and ranking criteria. The selecting official may select from any of the candidate lists. You should list any relevant performance appraisals and incentive awards in your resume as that information may be taken into consideration during the selection process. If selected, you may be required to provide supporting documentation. Selection is subject to restrictions resulting from Department of Defense referral system for displaced employees. If you have retired from federal service and you are interested in employment as a reemployed annuitant, see the information in the Reemployed Annuitant information sheet. You may claim Military Spouse preference. Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP). If you are a Federal employee in the competitive service and your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority for this position. To receive selection priority, you must: (1) meet ICTAP eligibility criteria (2) be rated well-qualified for the position and; (3) submit the appropriate documentation to support your ICTAP eligibility. To be considered well-qualified and receive selection priority applicants must satisfy all qualification requirements for the position and receive a score of 90 or above. Additional information about the program is on OPM's Career Transition Resources website.

Responsibilities include staff development of theater planning initiatives related to overall personnel support and sustainment functions and activities (OPLANS, CONPLANS, NEO).
Details.SubAgencyName: Headquarters United States European Command, Directorate of Manpower and Personnel
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, its impressive gardens and parks, palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles, but also by its cultural diversity. It is the home to USAG Stuttgart, HQ US EUCOM, HQ US AFRICOM, and other tenant units. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/
MajorDuties: Develop planning initiatives for personnel support in joint operations and multinational organizations.

Conduct substantive and complex analyses on a variety of long-range personnel planning issues regarding the entire spectrum of personnel support for theater missions as they relate to war and theater-engagement activities.
Engage with the deliberate planning cell in USEUCOM for development of primary personnel annexes and supporting documents.
Serve as an authoritative decision-maker during the planning process and represent the command when dealing with personnel support missions.
Prepare and staff annexes for all planning documents produced by the command.
Conduct extensive coordination with components, Joint Staff and other appropriate agencies to consolidate planning input into the appropriate planning documents.
Prepare expert input to a wide variety of theater planning documents.
Develop new initiatives for personnel support and policies regarding wide scope non-traditional missions.
Coordinate with Joint Staff and components for an integrated development of personnel support responsibilities.
Work with action officers at all levels to develop, integrate and document standardized personnel support policies and requirements.
Serve as advisor and assistant to the Division/Branch Chief.

Lead and provide advice to nine O-6/GS-15 equivalent division chiefs and staff to take necessary corrective steps or make modifications to proposals to ensure compliance with command and directorate policy or provide improved results.
Responsible for management of the government service and military staffing for the directorate in accordance with executive orders and applicable laws and regulations.
Confer with the director, deputies, nine division chiefs, senior enlisted leaders, and key directorate staff regarding problem areas and projected major changes in the assigned mission.

Coordinate the efforts of the nine divisions in policy development, preparation of plans and guidance, and analysis and evaluation of operations program performance in support of the command's strategic objectives for the five regions of Africa.
Plan for short- and long-term operations for the directorate.

Details.OtherInformation: Direct deposit of pay is required. U.S. citizens overseas under ordinarily resident status are not eligible for appointment under the Status of Forces Agreement. If an employee brings a child to an overseas location and that child is entitled to attend a DoD school on a space-required basis in accordance with DoDEA Regulation 1342.13, the DoDEA and the Military Department responsible for providing related services will ensure that the child, if eligible for special education, receives a free appropriate public education, including related services pursuant to DoDI 1342.12 and DoDM 1342.12. If an employee brings an infant or toddler (up to 3 years of age) to an overseas location, and that infant or toddler, but for the child's age, is entitled to attend the DoDEA on a space-required basis in accordance with DoDEA Regulation 1342.13, then the Military Department responsible for EIS will provide the infant or toddler with the required EIS in accordance with the eligibility criteria consistent with DoDI 1342.12 and DoDM 1342.12. Employees (and family members) who require medical or dental care in the overseas location will be responsible for obtaining and paying for such care. Access for civilian employees and their families to military medical and dental treatment facilities is on a space-available and reimbursable basis only. Pay retention may be offered to selected applicants for positions at overseas locations. Pay retention will not be offered as an incentive for employees moving between overseas positions. Selectees may receive certain foreign area benefits such as: Living Quarters Allowance (LQA) or government quarters, home leave, etc. Selectees will have their eligibility for foreign area benefits determined at the time of hire in accordance with Department of State Standardized Regulation (DSSR) and DoDI 1400.25 volume 1250. For positions in a foreign country, that country's laws or international agreements may have a direct impact on the ability of an employee's same sex domestic partner or spouse to accompany the employee and receive certain benefits. Time-limited promotions may be extended up to a maximum of five years. Time-limited reassignments and changes to lower grade may exceed five years, however return rights may be impacted. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Administration and Management Information Management Planning and Evaluating Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-12).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves as the Mission Assurance (MA) and Antiterrorism/Force Protection (AT/FP) subject matter expert, provides detailed and informed technical advice to the Commander, Special Operations Command Europe (SOCEUR), the SOCEUR headquarters staff, and subordinate unit commanders as required concerning all MA-related actions and activities across the U.S. European Command mission sets within the 51-country area of responsibility (AOR).
Details.SubAgencyName: Headquarters United States European Command, Special Operations Command Europe
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, its impressive gardens and parks, palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles, but also by its cultural diversity. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/
MajorDuties: Manage SOCEUR AT/FP activities and guides subordinate or assigned programs and serves as Command point of contact for coordination with other Commands and U.S. Government agencies.
Serve as the MA advisor and staff analyst for wartime emergency and contingency planning and peacetime missions for SOCEUR.
Serve as a senior AT/FP advisor and staff analyst for wartime emergency and contingency planning, peacetime missions for SOCEUR.
Serve as a key member of various US European Command, US Special Operations Command and SOCEUR Threat Working groups and maintains current knowledge of developments in evolving security technologies.
Identify, prioritize, and lead local threat, vulnerability, and risk assessments in support of Command and Component garrison, exercise, and operational plans.
Research, write and assist with the development and implementation of the AT/FP Plan and Program.

Review and analyze Department of State, Department of Defense, US European Command, and SOCEUR emergency, contingency and wartime/peacetime operation issues/plans and translates the results into policies, standards, and guidelines.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Incumbent will serve as a Nuclear Policy and Plans Specialist for the US European Command (EUCOM), Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) Division (J-5), responsible for coordinating and contributing to all NATO nuclear policy documents and initiatives in close coordination with the US mission to NATO, the Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), and Joint Staff. Represents the command at NATO nuclear committees at NATO Headquarters in Brussels, Belgium.
Details.SubAgencyName: Headquarters United States European Command, J5-8 Plans and Policy Directorate
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, its impressive gardens and parks, palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles, but also by its cultural diversity. The city of Stuttgart comprises five counties encompassing 179 towns and rural districts. It is the home to USAG Stuttgart, HQ US EUCOM, HQ US AFRICOM, and other tenant units. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/
MajorDuties: Develop command nuclear policy and strategy in close coordination with Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), Joint Staff, and US Strategic Communications Command (STRATCOM).
Participate in the command nuclear planning and integration of nuclear concepts into operation/concept plans (OPLAN/CONPLAN).
Represent the command at NATO nuclear committees at NATO Headquarters in Brussels, Belgium.
Provide briefings to inform senior leaders on nuclear policy issues for high-level meetings with OSD, Joint Staff, interagency, and NATO.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS GS-14 , if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service as listed below: Serving as an authoritative expert in exercise planning and information sharing initiatives across Department of Defense. Providing expert planning, cogent advice, oversight strategies and implementing recommendations from concept development through executive decision-maker program approval. Served as a Senior level exercise planner responsible for strategic recommendations and direction on complex and consequential matters at the Combatant Command and Service Component level. Details.JobSummary: This position is being filled under DoD Modified Direct Hire Authority, Section 1109; PL, 116-92, dated 12/20/2019. This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for serving as a Coalition Program Integration and Planning Specialist in the Joint Staff J6 Directorate, Coalition Coordination Branch, Coalition Interoperability Division, of the Deputy, Director for Cyber and C4 Integration.
Details.SubAgencyName: Command, Control, Communications & Computers (C4) and Cyber Integration (J6)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement J-6: The J-6 (C4 & Cyber) represents the Joint Warfighter in support of the command, control, communications, and computers/cyber (C4) requirements validation and capability development processes while ensuring joint interoperability. Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The position is located in the Joint Staff (JS) J-7 Joint Force Development Directorate, Deputy Directorate Joint Warfighting Development (JWD), Futures and Concepts Division (FCD), Suffolk, Virginia.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The DD JWD mission is to develop joint operating concepts and doctrine, educate the Joint Force, synchronize allies and partners joint force development programs, and integrate exercises, wargames, and experiments.
MajorDuties: As a CONOPS ANALYST at the GS-0301-14 some of your typical work assignments may include: The incumbent is responsible for reviewing and supporting the development of future Joint Concepts, developing CONOPS that apply the Joint Concepts against real-world operational problems, and supporting the design of the applications of the CONOPS into analytic activities such as wargames, Table-Top Exercises (TTX), and analytic studies including but not limited to sustainability, maneuver, fires, command and control and capabilities. The incumbent develops CONOPS that represent the central idea, operational approaches, and concept required capabilities in joint concepts for the purpose of evaluation and development of joint force development and design recommendations. Incumbent participates in seminars, meetings, workshops, conferences, panels, working groups, assessments, studies, concept evaluations, wargames and exercises related to the development and evaluation of joint concepts and development of CONOPS with participants from the Joint Staff, U.S. Combatant Commands, Combat Service Support Agencies, Services, interagency, Office of the Secretary of Defense, and multinational partners.

Provide results of studies, analyses, and evaluations to counterpart agencies to share experiences and thereby improve overall defense level planning in areas of assignment.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-14 grade level, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service: Applying analytical and evaluative methods and techniques to resolve issues and/or conduct studies concerning systems modernization in a joint and mission partner environment; Administering pertinent regulations, policies, and precedents that affect the combat development process to effectively direct and coordinate the efforts of team members from the senior military organizations; Reviewing and approving the integration of materiel solutions to capability deficiencies by applying Requirements Determination Processes, battlefield principles and concepts, standard integration practices and methods. Utilizing concepts of joint, service and mission partner and warfighting systems, command and control, joint interoperability and integration, and related DoD, service, and agency policies, regulations, and practices Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: Part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Serving as Management and Program Analyst providing command and control and operational expertise in direct support of the Requirements and Implementation Branch Chief, Coalition Interoperability Division (CID). Serves analytical expert for the assessment, synchronization and integration of joint and mission partner warfighting development functions and activities to address capability needs and interoperability shortfalls.
Details.SubAgencyName: Command, Control, Communications & Computers (C4) and Cyber Integration (J6)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Mission Statement: The J-6 (C4 & Cyber) represents the Joint Warfighter in support of the command, control, communications, and computers/cyber (C4) requirements validation and capability development processes while ensuring joint interoperability. To further this effort, the J-6 promulgates guidance and provides functional expertise to the Chairman in order to shape the joint information environment. Additionally, as the Joint Staff Chief Information Officer (CIO), the J-6 provides business class Information Technology (IT) services and support to the Chairman and the entire Joint Staff.
MajorDuties: As a MANAGEMENT AND PROGRAM ANALYST (INTEGRATION INTEROPERABILITY at the GS-0343-14 some of your typical work assignments may include: Serve as an operational and technical expert responsible for planning, execution and analysis of assessments and test and evaluations in support of the Requirements and Implementation Branch Chief and the Coalition Interoperability Division (CID) Chief. Participate in joint mission environment development of joint C2 capability test and evaluation standards and policies. Participate in the resource programming and budgeting process for the Division's efforts supporting the Department of Defense joint command and control family of programs, systems, and capabilities. Participate in the planning, direction, and coordination of functions such as review and recommended action on proposals, actions, and reports relative to program execution including recommendations for action or decisions by higher authority. Provide results of studies, analyses, and evaluations to counterpart agencies to share experiences and thereby improve overall defense level planning in areas of assignment.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serves as Lead Plans Specialist, responsible for developing, writing, and implementing armistice, contingency, and exercise plans of the garrison within guidelines provided by Headquarters (HQ) Installation Management Command (IMCOM), United States Forces, Korea (USFK), Eighth Army and the 19th Expeditionary Sustainment Command (ESC). NOTICE: Please carefully read ROK entry requirements in "How to Apply" section.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Daegu, South Korea within Area IV in the southern enduring hub for the US Army in South Korea. USAG-Daegu encompasses the southern third of the Korean Peninsula and Area IV is home to some 10,000 soldiers, KATUSAs, Sailors, Marines, Airmen, Civilians, Retirees, and their families. Daegu is a world-class city that has hosted the FIFA World Cup games and the International Track and Field Championships. "Colorful Daegu" is a world leader in energy conservation technology and development. Daegu is also known as the fashion capital of Korea and the Apple City. For additional information about Daegu and South Korea, please visit these links: http://english.daegu.go.kr/ and http://www.visitkorea.com/. NOTICE: Please carefully read ROK entry requirements in "How to Apply" section. NOTICE: Access to Medical and Dental care in Taegu is limited. Please see "Additional Information" below.
MajorDuties: Writing garrison supporting operations plans (OPLANs), operation orders, and implementing instructions to support United States Forces Korea, Eighth Army and 19th Expeditionary Sustainment Command OPLANs.
Converting planning directives into practical implementation guidance for the garrison and its subordinate elements.
Performing studies to analyze projected mission changes and determining appropriate armistice, contingency, or exercise plan modification.
Coordinate with force management to organize manpower and equipment requirements in support of garrison OPLANs.
Planning for Theater Readiness exercises, Non-combatant Evacuation Operations exercises, Antiterrorism exercises and Homeland Security Exercises Evaluation Program exercises.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-12, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes expert knowledge in the industrial, acquisition, and R&D fields, with highly comprehensive experience in the direction and management of research, development, procurement, production, and logistical activities associated with the broad field of armaments programs. Specific knowledge is required with respect to U.S. and Israeli acquisition laws and practices; technological, economic, and industrial base factors in defense acquisition; and the methodology for the initiation and establishment of international cooperative agreements for research, development, production, procurement, and logistical support. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-12 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-13 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of the laws, principles, policies, and practices of systems acquisition. Knowledge of the mission, roles, functions, organizational structure, management, and operation of large organizations to provide high level staff guidance and participate in the development of goals, objectives, and policies. 2. Knowledge of the relationships between HQ USCENTCOM and various U.S. Government agencies and departments, including the DoD, DoS, and their subordinate agencies and commands. 3. Knowledge of a wide range of qualitative and/or quantitative methods for the assessment and improvement of security assistance plans and procedures. 4. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures. 5. Ability to analyze, plan, and adjust work operations of one or more organizational segments to meet program requirements and objectives within available resources in support of research, development, production, and support of a system, subsystem, or equipment. 6. Ability to communicate both orally and in writing, clearly, concisely, and with technical accuracy. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Looking to make a difference? Join our team! Army Materiel Command (AMC) is the Army's primary logistics and sustainment command, responsible for managing the global supply chain and ensuring installation and materiel readiness across the Total Force. AMC is one of the Army's largest commands with nearly 165,000 military, Army Civilian and contractor employees, impacting all 50 states and more than 150 countries. Since 1962, AMC has played a significant role in supplying our forces during wars, conflicts and contingencies, and providing humanitarian aid and disaster relief. From managing the Army's global supply chain to providing quality of life programs for Soldiers and families; from providing financial management and contracting capabilities to leading the way in data analytics, AMC's missions are wide ranging and critical. AMC's workforce is at the core of the command's support to the Warfighter. If you are ready to take your career to the next level and be part of a culture that puts people first, we have an extensive array of career paths available. Join today and be the power behind ensuring the best equipped and sustained fighting force in the world.

Ability to analyze complex data sets, draw meaningful conclusions, apply analysis, evaluation, fact- finding, and investigative techniques to gather data, identify significant factors, and recommend a solution from several alternatives. 2. Skilled in coordinating resources and timelines to ensure successful program implementation. 3. Ability to provide leadership with insights to support strategic decision-making processes. 4. Knowledge of management analysis principles, concepts, and theories and the standard practices, methods, and techniques to perform complex but well-precedented assignments. 5. Ability to communicate clearly and concisely with technical accuracy, both orally and in writing, and work professionally with peers and management-skilled in effectively communicating technical information to diverse audiences. 6. Ability to build and maintain positive relationships with internal and external stakeholders. 7. Skill in identifying issues and proposing effective solutions by using knowledge of evaluating and improving organizational policies and procedures. 8. Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines while maintaining quality and accuracy (Time management and prioritization). WORK ENVIRONMENT: The work areas are adequately lighted, heated, and ventilated. The work environment involves everyday risks or discomforts that require normal safety precautions. Some employees may occasionally be exposed to uncomfortable conditions in such places as research and production facilities. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Online Application: Questionnaire Resume: For qualification determinations your resume must contain hours worked per week and dates of employment (i.e., month/year to month/year or month/year to present). If your resume does not contain this information, your application may be marked as insufficient and you will not receive consideration for this position. If you are a current Federal employee or previous Federal employee, provide your pay plan, series and grade, i.e. GS-0301-09. Current Federal Civilian Employees should list any relevant performance related rating (given within the last three years) and/or incentive awards in your resume. Do NOT include photographs (or links to social media such as LinkedIn), inappropriate material, inappropriate content, nor personal information such as age, gender, religion, social security number, etc., on your resume. To ensure full consideration of your experience and education we encourage you to use the USAJOBS resume builder to prepare your resume or to guide you in preparing your resume. Transcripts/Registration/License: If qualifying on education/position requires education, you must submit copies of your transcripts and if required for the position, submit an active, current registration/license. Veterans: If claiming VEOA, VRA or 30% Disabled Veteran - Submit VOW certification memo or copy of the official DD Form 214, which must include the character of service (i.e., with an honorable or general discharge). This will be annotated in block 24 on member copy 2, 4, or 7 of the DD Form 214. If claiming 30% Disabled Veteran, you must also submit a VA Letter or a disability determination from a branch of the Armed Forces. NOTE: All veterans claiming 10-point preference must also submit a SF-15 form. Current or Former Federal Civilian Employees (includes current Air Force employees): You must submit a legible copy of a SF-50, Notification of Personnel Action. The SF-50, block 24 must contain "1" or "2" AND block 34 must be a "1". Employees eligible under an OPM approved interchange agreement, block 34 may contain a "1" or "2". Promotion Consideration: If you wish to be considered as a promotion candidate and your SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you meet the one-year time-in-grade requirements. Appointment of military members before the release or discharge date is permissible if the member is on terminal leave. At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form 214 must be submitted upon receipt.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in which includes staff operations management concepts, principles, and methodologies and of qualitative and quantitative techniques for analyzing and measuring effectiveness, efficiency and productivity of administrative and technical programs. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of and ability to apply a wide variety of procedures, requirements, regulations, and policies related to specialized projects in the installation administrative, management and support work of a directorate Comprehensive knowledge relative to organizational structure, function and mission of wing and HQ Leadership ability including the ability to coach, mentor, and challenge others, ability to adapt leadership style to a variety of situations; ability to model high standards of honesty, integrity, trust, openness, and respect by applying these values on a daily basis Technical ability to conduct research, analyze a wide variety of programs/policies/procedures, evaluate program effectiveness/efficiency, recognize problems/weaknesses/constraints and impacts on other programs, summarizes results in order to make appropriate recommendations/changes and develop short term and long range administrative and management support plans Ability to communicate effectively, both orally in writing by providing accurate and effective staff summary analysis and briefings/presentations to all management levels PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. This is an acquisition demonstration project position NH-03 equivalent to a GS-12 to GS-13. Click here to view the AF Civilian Employment Eligibility Guide: AF DCIPS Interchange AF Internal Employee DoD Transfer (Excluding Air Force) EO 12721 Certain Former Overseas Employees EO 13473 Appointment of Certain Military Spouses Former Federal Employees (Reinstatement) Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Employee Military Spouse Preference Non-DoD Transfer PPP DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technicians PPP DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible PPP Mil Res (MR) and Nat Guard (NG) Pref Eligible Technician Receiving Disability Retirement Veterans Employment Opportunities Act
MajorDuties: Serves as the technical authority that oversees the development, implementation, operation and provision of the organizations administrative and management functions. Exercises delegated authority to develop and recommend administrative program and policy changes to ensure compliance with applicable guidance and direction. Gives advice, counsel or instruction to Directorates management. on both work and administrative matters, rejecting work projects and staff summary analyses back to the organizational focal points/management for corrective actions. Maintains the Director's calendar of events and requirements. Representing the Director, attends local installation, community and HQ meetings and conferences, in order to relay information, receive information or give input to important Installation operating issues, activities and events. Conducts special projects and studies, accomplishing research, providing qualitative and quantitative analysis of a fact-finding, investigative nature, relative to a variety of complex management or administrative issues to AF standards support compliance. Promotes safety and health in workplace through awareness and compliance with safety rules, regulations and best practices.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: CNIC offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. CNIC provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. The mission of the Fleet and Family Readiness (FFR) Programs is to maximize the physical, emotional and social development of the fleet, fighter and family. FFR enables a ready Navy force through its Fleet Readiness, Family Readiness, and Housing Programs. We provide direct and support services to all non-appropriated fund (NAF) employees who work for Morale, Welfare and Recreation (MWR) throughout the FFR Program worldwide.
MajorDuties: Report for duty with responsibilities as prescribed by the Bar or F&B Manager. Incumbent shall be familiar and comply with the contents of the Navy Food and Beverage Desk Guide and CNIC Instruction 1710.3, as well as all Hotel SOP's and instructions. Maintain proper decorum throughout events in accordance with prescribed rules and regulations. Shall be responsible for familiarizing him/herself with bar programming during duty shift, e.g., including any and all particulars that he/she should be cognizant of during the work shift. Check all schedules when entering duty. Ensure that activities take place as planned with proper equipment, personnel, food and beverages. In case of deviation from usual operating policy or procedures, bring the situation to the attention of the proper supervisor. Attempt to resolve the problem and, in case of a serious problem, contact the Bar or F&B Manager. Circulate among patrons as necessary to assure satisfactory services. Ensure we execute the services at the highest quality. Provide support and direction to ensure high quality of products and service is well executed. Explain and enforce hotel policies, procedures and regulations. Maintain order in the facility. Insures that local rules and regulations governing the sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages are strictly enforced. Incumbent may serve as a lead in assuring that work assignments by the shift employees are performed; provide necessary assistance and supplies to employees; and resolve minor problems and complaints of the employees, Make recommendations to the Manager regarding the work performance of shift employees. Prior to the end of each event, complete fire safety checks and that unnecessary electrical equipment are unplugged. Secure all doors, check all locks on the storerooms, etc. Assists with the stocking of supplies in the Bar. Ensure all equipment are properly stored and handled with care. Insure that all keys are properly secured. Incumbent must present a neat, well groomed, professional appearance at all times and must work harmoniously with co-workers and members of the Food & Beverage Department. Performs other related duties as assigned.

Please refer to: refer to: https://m.keta.go.kr/.DoD Civilians, their eligible family members and eligible military family members on official travel using a US passport must have either a Special Issuance Passport (SIP) or, as a temporary measure, a memorandum from a DoD Passport Agent stating the SIP application was submitted prior to departure from the point of origin. The memorandum must identify each applicant, date of submission, country of travel for PCS/TDY /TAD and DoD Visa Passport Automated System (VPAS) ID.After applying for an Official Passport and if it cannot be obtained prior to departure, use of a Regular (blue) Passport in lieu of the Official Passport is permissible for travel via MILAIR, contract and commercial air. Upon receipt of the SIP, traveler must coordinate with the DoD Passport Agent in country to ensure the proper visa and SOFA Stamp is placed on the SIP within 90 days of arrival in country by ROK Immigration officials.Non-US passport users and non-Korean passport users must comply with ROK requirements. Details.JobSummary: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. This National Guard position is for a FAMILY PROGRAM SPECIALIST, Position Description Number D1743000 and is part of the KS Joint Forces Headquarters, National Guard.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: THIS IS A NATIONAL GUARD TITLE 32 EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITION. The National Guard is the oldest component of the Armed Forces of the United States. Since the earliest American colonial days, citizens have joined together for collective defense. We have a proud tradition of coming to the aid of our friends and neighbors in times of serious emergencies. Join our National Guard team and serve your nation, your states and your community!
MajorDuties: A FAMILY PROGRAM SPECIALIST, GS-0301-09, is located in the Kansas Joint Force Headquarters, Manpower and Personnel Directorate (G1), Support Programs Division. The primary purpose of this position is to serve as a team member and advisor on Family Program issues, assist in the development, planning, implementing, and administering the Family Program concerning family and quality of life issues. Serves as an advisor on quality of life and Family Program matters for National Guard and reserve members with the goal of maximizing retention and readiness. Assists in the development, planning, and implementation of the Family Program, which includes readiness, volunteer management and improving the quality of life and well-being of members and families. This includes issues involving benefits, entitlements, scheduling events, missions, roles, and functions of the National Guard. Assists in planning, maintaining, and updating an ongoing system of information and referral for use by the military community. Coordinates dissemination of information. Prepares and disseminates information to staff and units to provide to family members and stimulate interest and support on benefits and entitlements. Conducts or assists in conducting seminars, conferences, and workshops as appropriate. Conducts needs assessments to identify other programming needs of family members. Assists in developing and maintaining local information and referral programs. Provides technical assistance to personnel publicizing quality of life and the Family Program. Conducts briefings and training for staff and units to stimulate interest, support, and provide necessary information. Provides technical assistance to personnel publicizing the Family Program. Receives and maintains volunteer hours contributed; supports Family Readiness Groups; designs and conducts training programs for volunteers; and designs and conducts volunteer recognition activities. Identifies key volunteers at the unit level to serve as volunteer coordinators. Develops standard formats and procedures to collect data. Initiates and provides technical assistance for the development of Family Readiness Groups. Identifies training programs and recognition activities for volunteers. Implements Guard Family Team Building (GFTB) and Guard Family Action Plan (GFAP) programs. Develops standard formats and procedures to record volunteer hours and to collect other volunteer related data. Identifies and maintains current listings of professional volunteer literature and training materials for the orientation for current and new volunteers. Serves as representative at conferences and meetings on quality of life and Family Program matters. As required, prepares, explains, and defends budgets relative to quality of life and Family Programs. Provides staff assistance to local units in accomplishing the objectives of the program. Conducts staff assistance visits to ensure that policies conform to guidance, to assist and gather information for new initiatives and direction. Provides technical interpretation and guidance. Plans and coordinates mobilization processes for pre-deployment, deployment, and post-deployment issues. Coordinates with local community resource agencies, i.e., active-duty installations, American Red Cross, and military health benefit administrators. Advises chain of command of current and proposed programs and policies requiring modification to improve family readiness and wellness. Ensures all recommendations are in accordance with applicable guidelines, policies, and regulations. Provides staff assistance and conducts visits to ensure policy guidelines are met. Coordinates the state family youth program that addresses issues and concerns of youth related to Guard life and youth readiness and well-being. Coordinates with local youth related organizations and agencies. Performs other duties as assigned.

MajorDuties: Serve as a Contracting Officer Representative (COR) for personal/non­ personal, medical services and support contracts.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a military technician position with the 99th Readiness Division, Reserve Personnel Advisory Center Staten Island Satellite, NJ016,Trenton, NJ. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This is a military technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Manages and provides technical advice and guidance regarding a wide variety of military Human Resources (HR) programs; Interprets, develops, implements, and administers a variety of staff assignments in various military HR program areas.
Analyzes significant military HR management issues and problems and develops recommendations and alternative solutions.
Provides guidance, interpretations, training and/or briefings on current and proposed policies to commanders, managers, and other key officials.
Manages and provides technical advice and guidance regarding the establishment and maintenance of pay accounts; processes, audits and edits of the complex pay actions.
Reviews master military pay account transactions and reports; Researches complex pay complaints and issues involving fraud, waste and abuse and responds or provides information.

Provides accurate and timely guidance to requests for information; Composes correspondence to clarify questionable areas; Compiles and analyzes data to identify trends, deficiencies and accomplishments.
Manages personnel, finance, and automated systems activities; Prepares reports and presents briefings.

Supervises the daily activities of personnel within the satellite center; Plans work to be accomplished by subordinates, sets and adjusts short-term priorities, and sets deadlines for completion of work; Assigns work to subordinates.

Gives advice, counsel, and instructions to employees on both work and administrative matters; Interviews candidates for positions in the organization and makes recommendations; Effects minor disciplinary measures.
Identifies developmental and training needs of employees; Provides or arranges for needed development and training.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is with the Defense Health Agency, Tripler Army Medical Center (TAMC), Directorate of Resource Management, Honolulu, Hawaii. Incumbent serves as Manpower and Management Analyst responsible for the areas of manpower and force management, manpower staffing criteria, analysis and approval process, distribution and documentation of manpower resources, various support agreements, Position Control Roster management, and timekeeping administration for TAMC.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: As an integrated health care system, the Defense Health Agency delivers healthcare services across the Department of Defense and enables combat support to the Joint Force as a strategic partner. Through a robust healthcare delivery system, and a dedicated team of inspired professionals, the Agency ensures the worldwide delivery of medical, dental, and pharmacy programs to more than 9.5 million uniformed service members, retirees, and their families, by improving health and building readiness Anytime, Anywhere-Always.
MajorDuties: Maintain Table of Distribution and Allowances (TDA) and Mobilization TDA or similar manpower database for an organization.
Prepare reports from Manpower databases (i.e. FMS Web, MEDTAADS) for staffing requirements and plans.
Maintain a time and attendance database system for employees of an organization to ensure personnel are being coded for attendance.
Manage In processing and out-processing of assigned personnel into or out of command-level data systems.
Provide manpower recommendations for realignments or reprogramming to assure continued mission accomplishment.
Perform command-level responsibilities to verify all Requests for Personnel Actions (RPAs) initiated within the organization.
Interpret regulations that affect current automation, security operations and Position Control Roster (PCR) management for assigned personnel.
Coordinate with lead personnel to review cost estimates, agreement validity, and stewardship of resources.
Review proposals for manpower adjustments in the capacity of a HQ or command-level resource management representative.
Prepare appropriate documentation of findings to support manpower recommendations via written and oral presentation.
Prepare standard operating procedures relative to system operations to ensure utilization and standardization occurs.
Prepare correspondence to inform all affected parties of the facts, agreed upon resolutions, outcome of costs analysis and interpretations of policy and regulatory guidelines.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes providing administrative assistance in support of a military unit or military activity in one or more of the following areas: unit or individual training, medical readiness, personnel actions, financial actions, supply, or logistics; performing day-to-day administrative functions; and preparing or reviewing written products. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Business Administration, Strategic Management and Organizational Design and Development. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Administration and Management Fundamentals and Operations of Military and Civilian Pay Organizational Awareness Technical Competence Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-07).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Military Technician position with the 79th Theater Sustainment Command, 658 Quartermaster Company, 365 Combat Sustainment Support Battalion, 321 Sustainment Brigade, 103rd Expeditionary Sustainment Command located in Tupelo, Mississippi. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This is a military technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Manage the daily operations of a US Army Reserve unit's mission readiness program
Represent the US Army Reserve Troop Program Unit Commander in his/her absence
Perform as the record manager
Serve as the unit physical security coordinator
Review regulations and directives and implements changes in appropriate manner
Compile data and create products to present at briefings
Prepare and review command correspondence for content and accuracy
Manage unit and individual personnel and medical readiness
Execute the unit's supply and logistics program
Coordinate the management of unit and individual training readiness
Administer financial management program including Government Purchasing and Travel Card programs
Advise on pay, benefits, entitlements, incentives, and assist with correcting pay issue

MajorDuties: MAJOR DUTIES: Responsible for the efficient operation of assigned areas with Temporary Lodging Facility operation. Performs full supervisory duties to include; initiating personnel actions, evaluating employees on their performance through consultation; verbal/written instructions and on the job training; assigning and distributing work; directing specific tasks and/or job assignments; performance appraisals and evaluations; nominations for employee awards; disciplinary actions; and related matters. Interviews personnel for employment and submit recommended selections. Responsible for scheduling, initial training, continuing instructions and efficient utilization of personnel within assigned area or department. Assist in maintaining records and files such as daily preparation of inventory reports, planning, budget preparation, scheduling or other related reports. Inspects area for compliance of fire, security and safety regulations that pertains to staff, correcting, discrepancies or reporting to Safety Coordinator. Conducts weekly inspections of area for cleanliness, maintenance and accountability of furnishings, correcting and/or reporting to Temporary Lodging Facility Manager. Establishes stock levels and conducts weekly inspection of inventory, prepares request for replenishment of stock to maintain levels established within budgetary parameters. Reviews daily occupancies of facilities and coordinates with Temporary Lodging Facility Manager in order to accurately plan for peak periods and rescheduling of staff to meet workload requirements. Prepares and certifies timecards for accuracy, resolving any discrepancies prior to submission for final review. Responsible for daily administrative work associated with the operations to include the preparation and submission of purchasing and operational records. Provides World Class Customer Service with an emphasis on courtesy. Assists customers and communicates positively in a friendly manner. Acknowledges customers, smiles and makes eye contact. Asks questions to determine, verify and solve problems. Checks for satisfaction on the quality of goods and services. Takes action to solve problems quickly. Alerts the higher-level supervisor, or proper point of contact for help when problems arise. Adheres to safety regulations and standards. Uses required safety equipment and observes safe work procedures. Promptly reports any observed workplace hazards, and any injury, occupational illness, and/or property damage resulting from workplace mishaps to the immediate supervisor. Adheres to established standards of actively supporting the principles of the EEO program and prevention of sexual harassment. Performs other related duties as required. CONTROLS OVER POSITION: Incumbent works under direct supervision of the Temporary Lodging Facility Manager who makes assignments by defining requirements, work priorities and task deadlines. The supervisor provides advice, assistance and support in unusual or controversial situations. Routine work is performed independently.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Planning, supporting, executing, and assessing service level training. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).
